text: Your commit history reads like a ransom note: 'fix', 'fix again', 'actually fix'.
You wrote 'minor changes' on a commit that touched 84 files.
Your most descriptive commit message to date is 'asdf'.
You force-push to main with the confidence of someone who has never read git log.
'WIP' has been in your commit messages since the last major version.
Your commits say 'final version'. There have been eleven final versions.
You committed node_modules and called it 'vendoring'.
Your commit message is just the ticket number, and the ticket just says 'see commit'.
